Header: Analeptes trifasciata (syn. Paranalentes reticulata ) (Branch girdler, stem girdler, Akyeekyee in Twi language)

Prevention: Prune dead wood above girdling level once in a year and burn outside the plantation to avoid pests build up.
Intercrop cashew with alternative host plants such as cassava to pull away the insect.
Regenerated side shoots due to girdling attracts foliar pests such as thrips and tea mosquito bug1.
Such side shoots should be pruned out.
Monitoring: The beetles feed by scraping the bark of stem and twigs and eventually break it into two.
The adult beetle is long horned and is about 4 cm long with orange-brown and black strips on the back.
The wounds created by scraping and girdling become suitable for egg laying by the beetles and endanger a tree to secondary infections.
Observe trees early in the morning and late in the evening for beetle activity.
Look for eggs below the bark above the girdled of the cashew branch that will hang or fall to the ground.
Look out for white to yellowish colored larvae of the size of matches stick on stems and branches.
Consider action when 2-5 trees in an acre of 40 trees are attacked.
When large number of branches on treetops are girdled beyond reach by hand, control measures might be too late.
Direct Control: Maintain farm sanitation by removing and burning girdled stems containing eggs and larvae of the pest.
All the hanging girdled branches and those that have fallen to the ground should be removed from the cashew plots on a monthly basis and burned.
Locate loose barks and spike out eggs and grubs and kill them.
Hand pick adult beetles from stem and branches and crash them dead.
